description: Killing parrots crashes your game. Note: I did kill other mobs and it isn t just swinging the sword and i got the same result everytime i killed a parrot. 19w40a: [^crash-2019-10-03_20.30.29-client.txt] Description: Unexpected error java.lang.NullPointerException: Unexpected error at atd.a(SourceFile:407) at axx.f(SourceFile:1234) at dmq.a(SourceFile:363) at das.aE(SourceFile:1234) at das.aG(SourceFile:1517) at das.n(SourceFile:1367) at das.d(SourceFile:907) at das.b(SourceFile:569) at net.minecraft.client.main.Main.main(SourceFile:199)
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft.
2. Create a new Singleplayer world with default settings.
3. Open the chat and enter the command ``/summon minecraft:parrot ~ ~ ~`` to spawn a parrot near you.
4. Select a sword in your hot‑bar.
5. Attack the summoned parrot until it is killed.
6. Observe that the game crashes and displays a java.lang.NullPointerException.
Observed Behavior: When the player attacks and kills a parrot the client crashes with a java.lang.NullPointerException, and this occurs consistently on every attempt regardless of the weapon used; the same action on other mobs such as zombies, skeletons or cows does not trigger the error. The crash appears in snapshot 19w40a and the attached crash report shows the exception originating in atd.a at line 407, followed by calls in axx.f, dmq.a, das.aE, das.aG, das.n, das.d, das.b and finally the main method in net.minecraft.client.main.Main. The stack trace indicates that a null reference is accessed during the processing of the parrot death event, causing the client to terminate. Multiple users have reported experiencing the identical failure, confirming that the issue is reproducible and not isolated to a single environment. The problem is limited to parrots; killing any other mob does not produce the NullPointerException.
Expected Behavior: When a player attacks a parrot and deals lethal damage, the parrot should be removed from the world, play its death animation, and drop any appropriate loot without causing any errors. The client should remain stable, allowing the player to continue playing normally after the kill, just as with other mobs in the game.
